interpretation: A three-day liminal/dark interval can arise from ordinary lunar visibility geometry; occurrence of the numeral 3 alone is therefore weak evidence for cross-cultural structural transmission.
source: Ancient Mesoamerica review of lunar visibility citing Schaefer; invisibility can span about 2.5, 3.5, or 4.5 days.

interpretation: Seven days approximates a quarter lunation, but numerical proximity does not establish that the biblical week derives from lunar quarters; modern scholarship explicitly disputes simple Babylonian-calendar derivations of the Sabbath week.

Coffin Texts spells 154-160 have been analysed as a chronologically ordered mythological account of the lunar month: invisibility, waxing, full moon, waning, last crescent, conjunction. This demonstrates that ancient religious/mythic texts can encode observable cyclic astronomy without implying the same mechanism in Genesis.

quantity: numerical modelling of periodic astral phenomena
interpretation: Mesopotamian astronomical traditions numerically schematized lunar visibility, daylight, eclipses, synodic appearances, and first lunar visibility. This establishes historical capability to represent celestial periodicity quantitatively.
